about: The dust a supply rocket's engine throws off the ground as it comes down beside the wreck, brought back on the owner's word (2026-10-12, 19:50: the wreck's landing dust comes back). The coordinator took it out on 2026-10-10 with the supply rocket and cargo lift that stood on the landing pad the owner rejected (data/scene/wreck.json owner_rejected, coordinator_removed); the pad stays out, so the dust now leaves the bare ground where the supply rocket's inventory row stands (data/inventory/wreck.json supply_rocket, its row dropped with the pad), and the rocket itself is not on the stage. The game 2099 drew it as 40,000 grains at 8 to 18 m/s rising at about 3 degrees (SupplyRocketView); the real footage this record is measured on shows something else: the Apollo landings' engine blast throws the dust out as one thin see-through veil racing out every way round, 1 to 3 degrees over the ground, at hundreds of metres a second, with no lone grains anywhere in it. So the dust is many fine soft cards streaming out fast and close over the ground. The world is a 220 m ball, so the ground falls away from the spot by the square of the distance over twice its radius; the bake pulls the veil down to follow it (the footage's sheet hugs the ground), and the footage gate measures how steeply the veil stands over the ground beneath each card, not over the spot's level.
rides_nothing: the supply rocket whose engine throws the dust is not on the stage (the coordinator took it out with the pad the owner rejected), so the dust leaves the ground where its row stands rather than riding it; when the rocket comes back it is placed `on` its prim
no_light: dust lifted off the ground gives off no light of its own; the sun lights it

effects.name: landing_dust
effects.from: footage: arxiv-2104.07669, arxiv-2305.12234, lpi-5040, arxiv-2306.01087 (the sheet 1 to 3 degrees over the ground: flatness 0.986 lets the cards out within 2.5 degrees of the ground's level either way, those below it hidden by the ground), arxiv-2102.12312 and nasa-alsj-a11-landing (one translucent veil streaming out radially, rocks seen through it, no lone grains: many soft dust cards, thin, growing as they fly), lpi-5040 and arxiv-2102.12312 (the finest dust at up to 3 km/s, sand at 100 to 1,000 m/s: 50 to 70 m/s here, slower than the real dust, so the 220 m world's curve can be followed: the pull of 16.4 m/s/s is 60 squared over the ball's 220 m, the ground's own fall-away for a card at the middle speed), arxiv-1503.00154 and nasa-a15-50yr (the blast reaching tens of metres out: the ring of the rocket's feet 3.3 m and body 2.0 m out to about 30 m in 0.4 s); game/world/supply_rockets/supply_rocket_view.gd:321-334,451-470 (the ring under the big rocket: feet 3.3, body 2.0, 0.1 high), game/outside/dust/dust_grains.gd:23-38 (REGOLITH #8b8883 lifted by GRAIN_LIFT 1.25 to #aeaaa4)

footage.how: Read off the papers' text (their measures made on the Apollo 16 mm descent films and the Surveyor III samples) and looked at on the descent frames they print. The angle is measured as the papers measure it, over the ground under the dust: here each card's height over the planned ground beneath it against how far along the ground it has gone from the spot (measure `rise`), 2 s into the stage's time, when the looped veil is whole.

arxiv-2104.07669.what: Immer, Lane, Metzger and Clements, Apollo video photogrammetry estimation of plume impingement effects (the 2008 conference version of Icarus 214:46-52, 2011; also NTRS-20130012063)
arxiv-2104.07669.measured: read in full and its frames looked at: the dust sheet's angle over the ground from how far the footpad's shadow stretches through it, Apollo 11 2.6 degrees, 14 2.4, 16 1.4, 17 2.0 (15 8.1 on an 11 degree slope); 1 to 3 degrees in general; the sheet partially transparent, faintest at its top

arxiv-2305.12234.what: Metzger and Mantovani, Damage to lunar orbiting spacecraft from lander ejecta
arxiv-2305.12234.measured: read: for most of a landing most ejecta travel in a cone 1 to 3 degrees over the local horizontal

arxiv-2306.01087.what: Metzger, Hintze, Trigwell and Lane, Further analysis on the Surveyor III dust deposits (also NTRS-20120000029)
arxiv-2306.01087.measured: read: the plume stays inside a 3 degree sheath before shut-off, the dust at most about 25 cm up 5 m from the nozzle; in the videos mostly a haze over the ground

arxiv-2102.12312.what: Understanding and mitigating plume effects (decadal white paper), its figure 1 an Apollo 15 descent frame
arxiv-2102.12312.measured: read, and the frame looked at: sheets blown out radially at 0 to 3 degrees at up to 3 km/s; in the frame an almost even bright grey-white veil filling the window with faint streaks, no lone grains

lpi-5040.what: Metzger 2020, Dust transport and its effects due to landing spacecraft, Lunar Dust 2020 abstract 5040
lpi-5040.measured: read: the finest dust up to 3.1 km/s, sand 100 to 1,000 m/s, gravel about 30 m/s; the sheet 1 to 3 degrees over the local ground

nasa-alsj-a11-landing.what: Apollo 11 Lunar Surface Journal, the landing, quoting Armstrong's 1969 debrief
nasa-alsj-a11-landing.measured: read: the dust first seen under about 30 m, 'a transparent sheet of moving dust' through which rocks could still be seen

arxiv-1503.00154.what: Lane and Metzger 2015, Apollo lunar dust transport from optical extinction (Acta Geophysica 63)
arxiv-1503.00154.measured: read: on Apollo 12 the dust and erosion start about 40 m up and reach about 65 m from the landing site; a 3 degree sheet

nasa-a15-50yr.what: NASA, 50 Years Ago: Apollo 15 at Hadley
nasa-a15-50yr.measured: read: dust first seen at about 37 m up, the view blocked by 15 to 18 m
